text_solutions.text: "• Statement I: Rotation of the earth shows effect on the value of acceleration due to gravity (g). This statement is TRUE. The Earth's rotation creates a centrifugal force that acts outwards, opposing gravity. This effect is small but measurable.<br \/>\n• Statement II: The effect of rotation of the earth on the value of 'g' at the equator is minimum and that at the pole is maximum. This statement is FALSE. The effect of the Earth's rotation is maximum at the equator and minimum (zero) at the poles. At the equator, the centrifugal force is directed directly outwards, having the greatest impact on reducing the effective gravity. At the poles, the axis of rotation passes through them, so the centrifugal force is zero."
